title: Fix the raced discriminator and silent reclamation in the Story 1.2 lock protocol
summary: Implement the two confirmed blockers from the F6-R2R3 post-fix review. F6-R4: the F6-R3 repair decides gone-versus-unparseable with a second stat taken after the failed read, so the discriminator itself can be raced into reporting a live successor's lock as unparseable and telling the operator to remove it; repair by reading the record once and judging those bytes, eliminating the second observation. F6-R9: afk_lock_reclaim can rename an abandoned lock aside, remove it, then lose the take to a contender and return 3 without ever emitting OPERATION_LOCK_RECLAIMED, because the reclaimed flag is only set on rc 0 — a silent destruction that contradicts the contract's reclamation-is-never-silent guarantee and makes the mutation gate fail 2 in 5 runs under load. Also restore gate integrity where the run-tests shellcheck sub-gate prints PASS from empty stdout when shellcheck fails to start, and align the two contract sentences the review falsified. Optionally, within the same established design: the cheap same-class repair for the evaluate existence/directory pair and the constructible CLI-level F6-R2 regression the review demonstrated. Preserve mutual exclusion, single-winner reclaim, exact-incarnation release, bounded acquisition, and all F6-R1/R2/R3 semantics. Add deterministic anti-vacuous regressions for each fix. Run all Story 1.2 gates including repeated mutation-gate runs under load, and git diff --check.
